reference.title: Staying Organized with Hierarchical Outlines [Planning & Game Design]
reference.transcriptScope: Complete Japanese auto transcript read; recognition errors are not verbatim-authoritative wording. Local research only.
reference.directVisualEvidence: CUA130 at 00:35 visibly identifies Smash Bros. Ultimate Main Menu and corresponding hierarchical outline.
reference.versionSelection: Retain Smash Ultimate, the same reference game. Independently recorded menu capture visibly shows 1.1.0; neither latest patch nor new mechanics are claimed.

referenceAlignment.retain: Introduce hierarchical outlines as a way to organize text and ideas.
referenceAlignment.ppt: Small unordered notes → headings and child items; define levels before use.

referenceAlignment.retain: Use the Smash Ultimate menu structure to show nested organization and opening children.
referenceAlignment.ppt: Match menu group to heading, show parent/child depth, expand one branch at a time; do not claim game-engine internals.

referenceAlignment.retain: Fighter → special move → specification; fold details and rearrange order/hierarchy.
referenceAlignment.ppt: Follow one editable branch, retain children while folding/moving, contrast display collapse with deleting content.

referenceAlignment.retain: Show where outline editing is available in Word.
referenceAlignment.ppt: Verify the actual current UI before naming menu steps; demonstrate only the relevant operations.

referenceAlignment.retain: Attribute Sakurai’s long use of outlines; distinguish personal organizing notes from a polished document for others.
referenceAlignment.ppt: Show the same content as working outline and reader-facing specification, without turning his experience into our biography.

referenceAlignment.retain: Broader use for organizing ideas, including channel planning; encourage trying the method.
referenceAlignment.ppt: End with a small practical outline exercise and return to the original conclusion; no unrelated game chapter.
